The failing test `ClassUtilsTest.test_getPackageName_Class()` is using the `ClassUtils.getPackageName` method to get the package name of a `String[].class` and expecting it to be `"java.lang"`. 

The current bug report describes that `ClassUtils.getShortClassName` is adding a semicolon to the end for all arrays. The example provided in the bug report shows that when calling `ClassUtils.getShortClassName` with an array, such as `sArray`, it returns the class name with a semicolon at the end, resulting in an incorrect output.

Looking at the method `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Object object, String valueIfNull)`, it checks if the object is null and returns the specified value if it is null. Otherwise, it calls `getShortClassName(Class<?> cls)` with the object's class. 

The method `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?> cls)` checks if the class is null and returns an empty string if it is null. Otherwise, it calls `getShortClassName(String className)` with the class name.

The issue seems to be in the `getShortClassName(String className)` method where the class name of an array is not handled correctly, leading to the addition of a semicolon at the end.

To fix this issue, the method `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String className)` needs to be modified to handle arrays properly and avoid adding a semicolon at the end when the class is an array type.

The root cause of the bug is the mishandling of array class names in the `getShortClassName` method, leading to the addition of a semicolon at the end.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
